$comment: Misconception catalogue. 'implicates' lists skills whose weakness this misconception is evidence of; the detour planner (src/engine/planner.ts) intersects it with the prerequisite closure of the failed skill. Awaiting named human review with the templates that use these tags.

misconceptions.description: Swaps the sides opposite and adjacent to an angle.

flashcard.front: In a right triangle, which side is adjacent to an angle?
flashcard.back: The side that touches the angle and isn't the hypotenuse. The opposite side is across from it.

misconceptions.description: Calls the hypotenuse the adjacent side.

flashcard.back: No: the hypotenuse is the longest side, opposite the right angle.

misconceptions.description: Uses sin for cos (or the reverse).

flashcard.front: sin θ or cos θ: which uses the side adjacent to θ?
flashcard.back: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse; sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.

misconceptions.description: Writes a trigonometric ratio upside down.

flashcard.back: No: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse (always at most 1).

misconceptions.description: Classifies a terminating decimal or a fraction as irrational (or the reverse).

flashcard.back: No: it is a ratio of integers. √2 is irrational.

misconceptions.description: Subtracts the magnitudes when finding the distance from a negative to a positive number.

flashcard.front: Distance from −3 to 5 on a number line?

misconceptions.description: Multiplies distance by speed to get time.
Divides speed by distance for time.
Divides the change in x by the change in y.
Judges steepness by the signed slope rather than its size.

flashcard.front: Which is steeper: slope −3 or slope 2?

misconceptions.description: Uses the height at one end for the area under a sloping line.

flashcard.front: Area under a sloping straight line?

misconceptions.description: Forgets the ½ in the area of a triangle.
Changes the sign wrongly when moving a term across the equals sign.

flashcard.back: Subtract 4 from both sides first: 3x = 15, x = 5.

misconceptions.description: Divides before removing the added term.

flashcard.back: Subtract b from both sides, then divide by a.

misconceptions.description: Keeps the wrong sign when making a variable the subject.

flashcard.front: Make a the subject of v = u + at.

misconceptions.description: Multiplies instead of dividing when isolating a variable.
Takes the roots of x² − (p + q)x + pq = 0 as −p and −q.
Uses b² + 4ac for the discriminant.
Forgets to square b in the discriminant.
Adds the horizontal and vertical gaps for a distance.
Halves the difference of the coordinates instead of averaging them.
Uses 360° as the angle sum of a triangle.

flashcard.front: Angles of a triangle add to?

misconceptions.description: Thinks alternate angles add to 180°.
Adds the two shorter sides to get the hypotenuse.

flashcard.front: Hypotenuse from legs a and b?

misconceptions.description: Adds the squares when finding a shorter side.

flashcard.front: Shorter side from c and a?

misconceptions.description: Uses degrees in s = rθ.

flashcard.front: Arc length s = rθ: θ in?

misconceptions.description: Uses the circumference formula for the area of a circle.
Uses the diameter in πr².

flashcard.front: Area of a circle of diameter d?

misconceptions.description: Believes a steady force keeps a body moving at constant speed on a frictionless surface.

flashcard.front: Unbalanced force on a body: effect?
flashcard.back: It accelerates: speeds up, slows down or turns.

misconceptions.description: Treats mass and weight as the same quantity.

flashcard.front: On the Moon, which stays the same: mass or weight?

misconceptions.description: Divides force by distance for work.

flashcard.front: Work done by a force F moving its point d along itself?

misconceptions.description: Thinks energy disappears as a ball falls.

flashcard.front: A falling ball loses height. Where does the energy go?
flashcard.back: Into kinetic energy (and a little into heat with air resistance).

misconceptions.description: Uses cos θ = 1 − sin θ.

flashcard.front: From sin θ to cos θ?
flashcard.back: cos θ = √(1 − sin²θ) for an acute angle.

misconceptions.description: Forgets the square root in cos θ = √(1 − sin²θ).
Swaps the standard values of sin 30° and sin 60°.
